questions.question: What was the best-selling color of toilet paper in the UK during the 1970s bathroom boom?
questions.note: Colored bathroom suites were fashionable, and toilet paper brands sold matching shades.

questions.question: Which food was once used as a movie theater seat-cleaning test because it left such stubborn stains?
questions.note: Its oil and color made it a practical stain challenge for upholstery.

questions.question: What did Victorian etiquette books warn guests not to do with asparagus at formal dinners?
questions.answer: Eat it with a knife and fork
questions.note: Asparagus was often considered acceptable finger food when served whole.

questions.question: Which everyday office object was patented with a design inspired by a bent hairpin?
questions.note: Many early clip designs relied on bent wire loops.

questions.question: What was the first product to be scanned with a retail barcode in a real shop?
questions.answer: A pack of Wrigley's chewing gum
questions.note: The scan happened in Ohio in 1974.

questions.question: Which animal was briefly used by the US military in a 1960s project to deliver listening devices?
questions.note: The project is often referred to as Acoustic Kitty.

questions.question: What strange item did some 18th-century Europeans wear in tall hairstyles to keep the shape overnight?
questions.note: Elaborate hairstyles could include structural frames and padding.

questions.question: Which soft drink was originally marketed as a brain and nerve tonic?
questions.note: Early advertising leaned heavily on medicinal-sounding claims.

questions.question: What was the original purpose of bubble wrap before it became packaging material?
questions.note: It failed as decor before finding its calling as protective packaging.

questions.question: Which household appliance had an early model nicknamed the Puffing Billy?
questions.note: Early powered cleaners could be large, loud, and engine-like.
